query: What is the date and content of the NIST page 'CAISI Works with OpenAI and Anthropic to Promote Secure AI Innovation'? Also the Anthropic blog 'Strengthening our safeguards through collaboration with US CAISI and UK AISI' and OpenAI's 'US CAISI / UK AISI AI update' - what dates were these published?
answer:
Report delivered. Key findings:

**Dates (all from source HTML metadata, not search snippets):**
- **NIST/CAISI page: September 25, 2025** (08:00 EDT, modified 14:12 EDT same day)
- **Anthropic blog: September 12, 2025** (tweet at 20:26 UTC)
- **OpenAI post: September 12, 2025** (tweet at 21:21 UTC) — note its actual title is "Working with US CAISI and UK AISI to build more secure AI systems"; `us-caisi-uk-aisi-ai-update` is just the slug
- Bonus: UK AISI companion post, September 13, 2025

**The finding that matters most for your base rate:** this was *not* a coordinated same-day tri-party release. The companies went first (55 minutes apart), UK AISI followed next day, and NIST posted **13 days later**, referring to the company posts in past tense.

**Base rate:** CAISI/US AISI has made exactly **3 joint announcements naming specific US frontier developers in ~24 months** — 2024-08-29 (Anthropic + OpenAI), 2025-09-25 (OpenAI + Anthropic), 2026-05-05 (Google DeepMind + Microsoft + xAI). Intervals of 392 and 222 days, mean ~307 days. All three were multi-company; none named a single lab in isolation. 106 days have elapsed since the most recent.

Worth separating from the much higher-frequency categories: CAISI *model evaluations* (~every 6-10 weeks, all targeting PRC models — DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM) and institutional/standards output (~monthly).

Two source caveats I'd flag: the NIST Sept 2025 page has **no Wayback snapshot at any date**, so dating rests on three internally consistent live metadata fields; and the May 2026 announcement **404s at its cited NIST URL and is absent from NIST's own CAISI news index** — confirmed instead via NIST's official GovDelivery bulletin and wire copy.

key_facts: The NIST page 'CAISI Works with OpenAI and Anthropic to Promote Secure AI Innovation' was published September 25, 2025 at 08:00 EDT (article:published_time = 2025-09-25T08:00-04:00), modified same day at 14:12 EDT.
Anthropic's blog 'Strengthening our safeguards through collaboration with US CAISI and UK AISI' was published September 12, 2025; its announcement tweet posted 2025-09-12T20:26:33Z.

OpenAI's post at slug us-caisi-uk-aisi-ai-update is actually titled 'Working with US CAISI and UK AISI to build more secure AI systems' and was published September 12, 2025; OpenAI Newsroom tweet posted 2025-09-12T21:21:20Z.
UK AISI published a companion post 'How we're working with frontier AI developers to improve model security' on September 13, 2025.

This was NOT a coordinated same-day tri-party release: the two company posts landed within ~55 minutes of each other on Sept 12, UK AISI followed Sept 13, and NIST posted 13 days later on Sept 25, describing the company posts in past tense ('recently published blog posts').

The NIST page is three short paragraphs with no original data: it frames CAISI's mandate under America's AI Action Plan, states CAISI worked with OpenAI and Anthropic to identify security issues and bolster AI security measurement in partnership with UK AISI, and notes continuing CAISI/UK AISI collaboration on metrology and standards.

CAISI/US AISI has made exactly 3 joint announcements naming specific US frontier developers in ~24 months: 2024-08-29 (Anthropic + OpenAI agreements), 2025-09-25 (OpenAI + Anthropic security collaboration), 2026-05-05 (Google DeepMind + Microsoft + xAI agreements).

Intervals between those three announcements: 392 days (Aug 2024 to Sep 2025) and 222 days (Sep 2025 to May 2026), a mean of ~307 days or roughly one every 8-10 months. 106 days have elapsed since the most recent as of 2026-08-19.
All three developer-collaboration announcements were multi-company; CAISI has never published a collaboration announcement naming a single US developer in isolation.

The May 5, 2026 release describes its new agreements as building on 'previously announced partnerships, which have been renegotiated' — implying the OpenAI/Anthropic MOUs were reworked in that wave, though neither company is named.

CAISI model-evaluation publications are far more frequent than collaboration announcements (~every 6-10 weeks) and target PRC models: DeepSeek (2025-09-30), Kimi K2 Thinking (2025-12-12), DeepSeek V4 Pro (2026-05-01), Z.ai GLM-5.2 (2026-07-17), UK AISI/CAISI joint on Kimi K3 (2026-07-23).
Two now-dormant individual pre-deployment evaluation posts exist from the AISI era: Anthropic's upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet (2024-11-19) and OpenAI's o1 (2024-12-18). No equivalents published since.
As of the May 5, 2026 announcement, CAISI reported having completed more than 40 evaluations, including on state-of-the-art models that remain unreleased. CAISI Director is Chris Fall.
The NIST Sept 2025 page has no Wayback Machine snapshot at any queried date; date verification rests on three internally consistent live metadata fields (OpenGraph, JSON-LD, rendered time element).

The May 5, 2026 CAISI announcement does not appear in NIST's own CAISI-tagged news search index and its cited NIST URL currently returns HTTP 404; it is confirmed instead via NIST's official GovDelivery bulletin and verbatim wire copy.
The Aug 2024 AISI/Anthropic/OpenAI agreements page carries dateModified 2026-05-04T15:30, one day before the May 5, 2026 announcement.

Anthropic's post details CAISI/AISI red-teaming of Constitutional Classifiers on Claude Opus 4 and 4.1, covering prompt injection bypasses via false human-review annotations, a universal jailbreak that prompted architectural restructuring, cipher-based attacks, obfuscation attacks, and automated attack refinement.

OpenAI's post details two novel CAISI-found ChatGPT Agent vulnerabilities chained into an exploit with ~50% success rate, fixed within one business day, plus UK AISI biosecurity red-teaming running May-August 2025 across ChatGPT Agent and GPT-5 that produced more than a dozen vulnerability reports.
